edits.modify_from: (3) go through the remaining frames; whenever a frame lists two containers at positions that are not slots (off by well over 10 pixels), a shuffle is under way between the two containers whose slots are now empty; it lasts until a frame again shows all containers at slots; at that frame those two containers have SWAPPED slots, so if the named container was one of the two, its slot is now the other container's old slot; a second shuffle of the same pair swaps them back; shuffles of other pairs do not change its slot;
edits.modify_to: (3) walk the frames after the first container frame in order and keep a running slot assignment. A SHUFFLE is a maximal run of consecutive frames in which two containers are off their slots (well over 10 pixels); it ENDS at the first later frame where all containers are again at slots. At that ending frame, swap the slots of the two containers whose slots were empty during the run. Keep walking: if a later frame again shows two containers off their slots, that is a NEW shuffle, even if it is the same two slots as before, and it swaps them again when it ends. Before computing the answer, write out the list of shuffles in order (e.g. 'shuffle 1: slots P and Q, frames 80-96, ends 112; shuffle 2: slots P and Q, frames 128-144, ends 160'). Two shuffles of the same pair put them back where they started; three leave them swapped. Shuffles of other pairs do not change the named container's slot;

edits.modify_to: (3) scan the frames after the first container frame in order and split them into runs: a run is a maximal block of consecutive frames in which two containers are away from their slots (off by well over 10 pixels, however their positions change inside the block), and it ends at the first following frame in which every container is again at a slot.
